title: Strings
summary: Text values wrapped in quotes: "hello". Strings are immutable, support concatenation with `..`, and have a rich string library for searching, splitting, and formatting.

details.heading: Writing strings
details.body: Double quotes `"hi"`, single quotes `'hi'`, or double brackets `[[multi-line]]`. Backslash escapes: `\n` newline, `\t` tab, `\"` quote, `\\` backslash. Luau adds interpolated strings: `` `Hello, {name}!` ``.

details.heading: Core operations
details.body: Concatenation `a .. b` (auto-converts numbers), length `#s`, indexing `s:sub(i, i)` (strings have no direct `[i]` access that returns a character), comparisons `<`, `==` (lexicographic).

explanation.whatItIs: A string is a sequence of characters — names, chat messages, asset paths, IDs. In Luau strings are *immutable*: operations like `upper()` return a new string instead of changing the original.
explanation.whyItExists: Games talk to players and to each other: UI text, messages, data keys, and remote payloads all rely on text.
whenToUse: Identifiers and keys: DataStore keys, CollectionService tags
whenNotToUse: Don't concatenate in tight loops — build a table of parts and use `table.concat(parts)` instead
Don't store numbers as strings 'just in case' — it forces conversions everywhere
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local name = "Raanis"
local greeting = "Hello, " .. name .. "!"   -- concat
local shout = string.upper(greeting)         -- new string

print(#name)        --> 6 (length)
print(name:sub(1,3)) --> "Raa"
```
Strings are chains of characters. Cutting and gluing always produces a *new* chain.
tips: `tostring()` turns any value into a printable string; `tonumber()` parses numbers out of strings
commonMistakes: Treating string indices 0-based or expecting `s[1]` to give the first character
Forgetting `tostring()` before `..`-ing nil or booleans errors only for nil: `"x" .. nil` errors

examples.title: Everyday string operations
examples.code:
local player = "Raanis"

print("Hello, " .. player)          --> Hello, Raanis
print(`Hi, {player}!`)              --> Hi, Raanis!  (interpolation)
print(#player)                      --> 6
print(player:upper())               --> RAANIS
print(player:sub(1, 3))             --> Raa
print(player:find("aan"))           --> 2  4
print(player:gsub("a", "o"))        --> Roons  2
print(string.split("a,b,c", ","))   --> {"a", "b", "c"}

examples.title: Formatting HUD text
examples.code:
local kills = 7
local timeLeft = 90

local label = string.format("Kills: %d | Time: %d:%02d", kills, timeLeft // 60, timeLeft % 60)
print(label)   --> Kills: 7 | Time: 1:30
examples.whyItWorks: `%d` inserts integers, `%02d` pads to two digits. `string.format` keeps number-heavy UI text readable.
